summary: Built as a 1932 L-4 on a crow's-nest site, replaced by a 1962 R-6 cab, unstaffed by the late 1960s, and it survived the 2021 Bootleg Fire.

facts.design: R-6 flattop cab (14 x 14 ft) on a 20 ft timber tower
facts.status_note: Listed as standing; a July 2024 visitor labeled it abandoned and said it needs a lot of work.

staffing.status: not regularly staffed since the late 1960s; placed on standby status in 1968 (NHLR)

access.note: No closure notice in the sources. A July 2024 visitor found the road to the trailhead open. The tower is not staffed or rented, and no source says the public may climb it.

visit.trail_note: From the Lookout Rock Trailhead at the end of Road 012, follow the old road up through burned timber. Some class 2 scrambling is needed to reach the base of the rock.

events.note: A newspaper item said a fireman from the Finley corrals would be placed on lookout duty at this site.
A 20 ft wooden tower with an L-4 cab replaced the earlier crow's-nest tree platform.
A July 18, 1947 item says Kenneth Carlson had been the forest lookout the previous summer, and the district still wanted a lookout for the post.
A regional engineering inspection recommended replacing the tower and house as soon as financing could be arranged.
The 1932 L-4 was replaced by the present 14 x 14 ft R-6 flattop on a 20 ft timber tower.
The NHLR says the lookout was placed on standby status in 1968. A 2024 visitor account says it was no longer regularly staffed by the end of the 1960s.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register on March 1, 2000.
The Bootleg Fire burned through the area. The tower survived, with some timber beams scorched.

corrections.why: Sources describe a 20-foot tower: firelookout.com says 20' treated timber R-6 flat tower, and the 1959 inspection says 20 feet in height. The current 10.7 m (about 35 ft) matches neither; no source gives a total structure height.

corrections.proposed: 1932 built (L-4 tower); 1962 replaced by present R-6 cab
corrections.why: The NHLR Built field gives 1962, but the site had a 20 ft L-4 tower from 1932 that the 1962 R-6 cab replaced.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR and the Forest Fire Lookout Association directory list it as standing; the July 2024 visitor calls it abandoned. The tower stands, and every source says it is not in regular use.
NHLR gives 6,419 ft (1,957 m); firelookout.com and the 2024 visitor give 6,508 ft. The record's 1,956.5 m is consistent with NHLR.

notes_for_editor: Current condition rests on one July 2024 visitor blog. No 2025-26 source was read. Forest Service pages were not fetched; a Fremont-Winema trailhead page appeared in search and was not read. The 1931, 1932 and 1947 newspaper items are only as transcribed on oregonlookouts.weebly.com; originals not checked. Unresolved: the 1932 Bend Bulletin item says the legs were sixteen feet high, while later sources say the tower was 20 ft; the story says the sources differ. Photos not added: no image URL with a confirmed license.
